subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw define and support a runtime-neutral agent-core protocol for no-Node embedded ports, or should this remain external prior art outside core?
rationale: Current code and docs still define OpenClaw as a Node-hosted TypeScript/Gateway runtime, and changing that boundary affects core architecture, plugin APIs, support scope, and long-term compatibility.

options.title: Keep canonical design tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open for an explicit runtime-neutral protocol/RFC decision before accepting any implementation.

options.title: Narrow to plugin or SDK seams
options.body: Split only concrete missing plugin or JSON-RPC seams into narrower issues while leaving MimiClaw-style ports external until core APIs exist.

options.title: Reject core no-Node support
options.body: Close this and document that embedded ports are independent projects, not supported OpenClaw runtime targets.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical design tracker
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for an explicit runtime-neutral protocol/RFC decision before accepting any implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is on runtime boundary and agent-harness direction, and the same person wrote prior keep-open review context for this issue.
